answer.worked:
Let $u=1-x^2$. Its possible values are $(-\infty,1]$. From the graph, $f$ is defined for every real input except $0$, so the permitted inner values are
$$(-\infty,1]\cap\bigl((-\infty,0)\cup(0,\infty)\bigr)=(-\infty,0)\cup(0,1].$$
For the domain,
$$\begin{align*}1-x^2&\ne0\\x^2&\ne1\\x&\ne\pm1.\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$\operatorname{dom}(g)=(-\infty,-1)\cup(-1,1)\cup(1,\infty).$$
For $u<0$, the negative branch gives every output in $(-\infty,0)$. For $0<u\le1$, the left side of the positive branch gives every output in $[2,\infty)$. The endpoint $2$ is included because $u=1$ occurs at $x=0$ and $f(1)=2$.
Therefore
$$\operatorname{range}(g)=(-\infty,0)\cup[2,\infty).$$
